preamble: In Tokyo Japanese the moraic nasal /N/, traditionally transcribed as uvular [ɴ] in utterance-final position (especially after back vowels /a, o/), can lose its oral closure and surface as a nasalized vowel whose quality copies the preceding vowel; after /o/ this gives a nasalized [o]-like vowel. The nasal-vowel realization is regular before vowels, glides and fricatives and occurs in about 5% of utterance-final tokens in real-time MRI data. This is synchronic allophony of a single phoneme and is not otherwise attested cross-linguistically.

examples.note: Before a vowel or word-finally /N/ is a moraic nasalized vowel or semivowel whose quality depends on the preceding vowel; MRI data show that most utterance-final tokens have a closure from palatal to uvular, conditioned by the preceding vowel, and about 5% have no closure at all.
Medial /N/ before a vowel realized as a nasalized vocoid rather than a stop closure (here after /a/).

sources: Maekawa, K. (2023). Production of the utterance-final moraic nasal in Japanese: A real-time MRI study. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 53(1), 189–212. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100321000050
Youngberg, C. (2021). Representing the moraic nasal in Japanese: evidence from Tōkyō, Ōsaka and Kagoshima. Glossa 6(1). https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1099
Vance, T. J. (2008). The Sounds of Japanese. Cambridge University Press.
